nodes.label: tasteskill v2 (design-taste-frontend skill)
nodes.rationale: Model-built pages average every page seen; the skill replaces defaults with decisions: dealt directions, subject-derived idea, measured house style, and a look-and-fix loop.

nodes.label: House rules for app screens
nodes.rationale: Page rules were written for pages read once; app screens are read daily, so borders, row rules, small labels and peer cards are relaxed within limits.

nodes.label: House rules (no-slop)
nodes.rationale: Some rules come from the study (icon cards, pills, gradients, shadows, tracked caps rarer on top sites); others (monospace labels, index numbers, hairline grids) are owner taste because generators imitate them.

nodes.label: Substance over restraint
nodes.rationale: Removing ornaments alone reads as thin; blind jurors prefer richer pages, so larger type, colour fields, real pictures and full content must replace them.

nodes.norm_label: study of 99 awwwards sites of the day (motion)

nodes.label: --ease-expo curve
nodes.rationale: Expo out ran on 14 studied sites, more than any other chosen family, and is the curve long reveals use.

nodes.label: No preloader, gate, custom cursor or scroll hijacking
nodes.norm_label: no preloader, gate, custom cursor or scroll hijacking
nodes.rationale: 60 of 99 sites opened on a loading screen yet half were unreadable 2.5s after load; hijacked scroll scored lower usability (6.01 vs 6.50).

nodes.label: Signature moves
nodes.rationale: Pick by subject; a move that says nothing about the subject is decoration.

nodes.label: 3D gallery (not built)
nodes.rationale: The one placement associated with lower scores (7.30 vs 7.44) and lowest usability (5.9 vs 6.35).

nodes.label: One live thing
nodes.rationale: Every winning page in blind tests had one interactive element made from the idea, and jurors named it first.

nodes.label: Motion budget
nodes.rationale: A static page reads as a mock-up; uniform motion says nobody decided, choreographed motion with one protected moment says somebody did.

nodes.label: The argument (claims with proof)
nodes.rationale: Claims decide which sections exist, avoiding the stock hero/logos/features/testimonial/pricing sequence.

nodes.label: Look-and-fix loop
nodes.rationale: Passing the gate only means nothing banned was measured; screenshots are judged with the critique rubric for up to three rounds.

nodes.label: Subject inventory
nodes.rationale: In blind tests, the winning page for each brief was built from an inventory item specific to the client; it also drives picture searches.

nodes.label: MCP Server Evaluation Guide
nodes.rationale: Server quality is measured not by how comprehensively tools are implemented but by how well they let a context-free LLM answer realistic, difficult questions.

nodes.label: Evaluation Answer Guidelines (direct string comparison)
nodes.rationale: Answers must be single, human-readable, diverse values verifiable by direct string comparison, not lists or complex structures.

nodes.label: Answer Stability (closed/historical data)
nodes.rationale: Avoid dynamic current-state counts (reactions, replies, members) so answers never change.

nodes.label: Five-Step Evaluation Creation Process
nodes.rationale: Documentation inspection, tool inspection, developing understanding, read-only content inspection, task generation; never read server implementation code.

nodes.norm_label: mcp error handling (tool errors in result objects)

nodes.label: Evaluation Question Requirements (10 independent read-only questions)
nodes.norm_label: evaluation question requirements (10 independent read-only questions)

nodes.label: Evaluation Question Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Questions must be independent, non-destructive, multi-hop, not solvable by keyword search, and stress-test tool return values to challenge context-limited LLMs.

nodes.label: CHARACTER_LIMIT by Returning Fewer Items (v2)
nodes.rationale: Never cut text; return fewer items so next_offset points at the first omitted item and JSON text still matches structuredContent.

nodes.label: Give the product a face
nodes.rationale: Judges' top complaint after four rounds: 'a well-applied kit, not a product with its own identity'.

nodes.rationale: Streamable HTTP for remote multi-client servers; stdio for local single-user tools, which must log to stderr not stdout.

nodes.rationale: Names should be general, descriptive of the service, easy to infer, without version numbers.

nodes.label: createServer() Server Factory
nodes.rationale: Return a fresh McpServer per call so HTTP stays stateless and scales horizontally; a shared instance fails concurrent requests with -32603. Keep the factory cheap by holding clients at module scope.

nodes.label: Per-request StreamableHTTPServerTransport (stateless, v1)
nodes.rationale: A new transport per request avoids request ID collisions.

nodes.label: Zod >=4.2.0 Requirement
nodes.rationale: v2 does not support Zod 3; Zod 4.0-4.1 schemas fail to type-check in registerTool and older versions drop .describe() text.

nodes.label: API Coverage vs Workflow Tools
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive coverage lets agents compose operations; workflow tools are convenient for specific tasks. When uncertain, prioritize comprehensive API coverage.

nodes.label: Four-Phase MCP Server Development Workflow
nodes.rationale: Research/plan, implement, review/test, then evaluate: server quality is measured by how well it lets LLMs accomplish real tasks.

nodes.label: Recommended Stack (TypeScript + Stateless Streamable HTTP / stdio)
nodes.norm_label: recommended stack (typescript + stateless streamable http / stdio)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript has high-quality SDK support, MCPB compatibility and models generate it well; stateless JSON Streamable HTTP is simpler to scale than stateful sessions; stdio for local servers.

nodes.label: TypeScript SDK v1 vs v2 Choice
nodes.norm_label: typescript sdk v1 vs v2 choice
nodes.rationale: v2 (@modelcontextprotocol/server) is current stable for new servers; v1 (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk) only gets bug/security fixes and is used only for existing v1 projects; never mix the two.
